course.title.value: Sites, apps and automations with AI

course.summary.value: Learn to talk to AI and create projects, one step at a time. This preview tests the new first lesson; the other 11 lessons keep their previous content.

notice.external-record.value: Tell us what happened. If you used the example, say so.

criterion.execution-record.value: I described what I managed to do or where I stopped.

criterion.compare-record.value: I checked the result described in this step.

workspace.summary.value: Follow an example conversation and learn to ask, read and check a reply.

workspace.outcome.value: Recognize a request, a reply and a simple correction.

workspace.access.objective.value: Write the word the AI replied with in the example.

workspace.access.hint.value: Claude and Codex are names of tools that use AI. Ganesha is where you are learning.

workspace.access.body.value: AI means artificial intelligence. In this lesson, it is a program that answers written messages. Example: a person writes “Say hello”; the AI replies “Hello!”. Its answer can contain mistakes. You can complete this entire lesson using the examples, without installing anything.

workspace.folder.title.value: Where to write and where to read

workspace.folder.objective.value: Write “in the message box” to show where a request starts.

workspace.folder.expected.value: Your note identifies where to write a request.

workspace.folder.hint.value: The appearance and button label vary between tools. The example teaches the sequence without requiring you to open a tool now.

workspace.folder.body.value: In an AI conversation, you write in the message box and use the send button. The reply appears in the conversation. Example: box → “Say hello” → send → reply “Hello!”. Here in Ganesha, the field below records your activity; it does not send requests to the AI.

workspace.fictional-brief.objective.value: Copy the school’s three types of lessons here.

workspace.fictional-brief.expected.value: Your note includes guitar, piano and singing.

workspace.fictional-brief.hint.value: You do not need to research anything or create files. All the information you need is in the text above.

workspace.fictional-brief.body.value: We will use a fictional school: Ponte Musical. It offers guitar, piano and singing lessons for beginners. This is the information we will give the AI. That way, you already know what its answer should say.

workspace.context-check.objective.value: Select the message that is the request.

workspace.context-check.expected.value: You can distinguish a request from a response.

workspace.context-check.hint.value: Look for the message written by the person before the AI response.

workspace.context-check.body.value: Look at this example conversation. Person: “Say hello”. AI: “Hello!”. The request is the text the person sends. The response is the text the AI sends back.

workspace.context-check.check.success.value: Right: the request comes from the person and the response comes from the AI.

workspace.context-check.check.retry.value: Check who wrote each message in the example.

workspace.context-check.feedback.b.value: Right: the person sent that request.

workspace.context-check.feedback.c.value: That field records the activity; it is not a conversation message.

workspace.select-context.objective.value: Write “I will use the example” or “I opened a conversation in the tool”.

workspace.select-context.expected.value: Your note shows which path you chose.

workspace.select-context.hint.value: No installation or subscription is required to follow the example. If you open the tool, look for the message box described in step 2.

workspace.select-context.body.value: You can learn by reading the example conversation in this lesson. If you already have access to Claude or Codex, you can also open that tool and start a conversation. You do not need a folder or file for this text request. If access or setup is required, continue with the example.

workspace.read-only-request.objective.value: Write “I read the example” or copy the reply that appeared in your tool.

workspace.read-only-request.expected.value: You have a reply to read, identified as an example or as a reply from your tool.

workspace.read-only-request.hint.value: If no reply appears, write what appeared on the screen. You do not need to fix everything now. The next step shows an example reply for us to check together.

workspace.read-only-request.body.value: This is the complete request for the AI. If you opened a tool, copy the request below into its message box and send it. If you chose the example, read the request and the example reply below it. In Ganesha, record which path you took.

workspace.read-only-request.prompt.value: Write two simple sentences about the school Ponte Musical. It offers guitar, piano and singing lessons for beginners. Include all three types of lessons. Do not create files or publish anything.

workspace.read-only-request.example.value:
EXAMPLE REPLY (with one detail missing):
Ponte Musical offers guitar and piano lessons. The lessons are for beginners.

workspace.compare-context.title.value: Did the reply leave something out?

workspace.compare-context.objective.value: Write the type of lesson missing from the example reply.

workspace.compare-context.hint.value: Everyone checks the same example in this step. If your tool mentioned singing, it got this detail right; you do not need to invent an error.

workspace.compare-context.body.value: Let us check this example reply: “Ponte Musical offers guitar and piano lessons. The lessons are for beginners.” The request included guitar, piano and singing. Compare the list with the reply: singing is missing. An AI reply can sound good and still forget some information.

workspace.access-recovery.objective.value: Copy the correction request shown in the example here.

workspace.access-recovery.expected.value: Your note says what to add and what to keep.

workspace.access-recovery.hint.value: In the tool, write a correction in the same message box and send it like the first request. You only need to send it if the reply has this problem.

workspace.access-recovery.body.value: You can continue the same conversation to ask for an adjustment. Example new request: “Include singing too. Keep guitar, piano and the name Ponte Musical.” Example corrected reply: “Ponte Musical offers guitar, piano and singing lessons. The lessons are for beginners.” Singing now appears.

workspace.access-evidence.title.value: What did you manage to do?

workspace.access-evidence.objective.value: Select the sentence that describes this person.

workspace.access-evidence.expected.value: The sentence recognizes learning from the example.

workspace.access-evidence.hint.value: Reading an example and receiving a reply in the tool are different experiences. Both can help you learn; your record should say which happened.

workspace.access-evidence.body.value: A person followed all the examples in this lesson but did not open Claude or Codex. They learned to recognize requests, replies and a correction. That is a valid result. Let us choose a sentence that describes what they did.

workspace.access-evidence.check.success.value: Right: you can learn from an example and record that path.

workspace.access-evidence.check.retry.value: The person followed the example without opening a tool.

workspace.access-evidence.option.a.value: “I received a reply in my tool.”

workspace.access-evidence.feedback.a.value: They did not open the tool.

workspace.access-evidence.feedback.b.value: The lesson showed a conversation; no website was created.

workspace.access-evidence.option.c.value: “I followed the example and learned how to request a correction.”

workspace.access-evidence.feedback.c.value: That describes learning from the example.

workspace.workspace-record.title.value: Keep one idea from this lesson

workspace.workspace-record.objective.value: Complete: “In this lesson, I learned that…”.

workspace.workspace-record.expected.value: You recorded one idea from the lesson in your own words.

workspace.workspace-record.hint.value: A short sentence is enough, such as “the request goes in the message box”. In the next lesson, we will practise explaining what we want more clearly.

workspace.workspace-record.body.value: You saw a request, a reply and a correction. The AI answered written messages, and we checked whether singing appeared in the reply. Example final note: “I learned that I need to check whether the AI included everything I asked for.”

requests.title.value: Write requests that guide the work

requests.summary.value: Outcome, data, boundaries, criteria and clarification.

requests.outcome.value: Write a bounded request and review a plan before execution.

requests.desired-result.title.value: Turn a vague idea into a deliverable

requests.desired-result.objective.value: Define what should exist when the task ends.

requests.desired-result.action.value: Write one sentence describing the deliverable you want.

requests.desired-result.expected.value: The sentence identifies a plan and the page’s purpose.

requests.desired-result.hint.value: Describe what you will receive, not only how you want to feel.

requests.desired-result.body.value: “Make something beautiful” does not define a verifiable deliverable. For Ponte Musical, the first result is a list-form plan for a presentation page, not the built page. Choosing a small deliverable makes comparison possible without understanding code. This structure supports the exercise; it is not a universal formula for requests.

requests.relevant-context.title.value: Select context that changes the answer

requests.relevant-context.objective.value: Include necessary context and exclude irrelevant information.

requests.relevant-context.action.value: Select the details the plan needs.

requests.relevant-context.expected.value: The list contains relevant details and declared gaps.

requests.relevant-context.hint.value: A missing detail can become a question, not an invention.

requests.relevant-context.body.value: Use the brief: fictional school name, beginner audience, guitar/piano/singing and contact. Another business’s opening hours or an old conversation does not help this goal. Explicitly identify missing important details. Asking the AI to invent the school’s location would produce an unsupported claim.

requests.complete-request.objective.value: Combine deliverable, context, boundaries and verification criteria.

requests.complete-request.action.value: Adapt the request and identify its main boundary.

requests.complete-request.expected.value: The request includes deliverable, data, boundary and future verification.

requests.complete-request.hint.value: Keep this lesson limited to planning.

requests.complete-request.criterion.1.value: Deliverable and necessary data are explicit.

requests.complete-request.criterion.2.value: The boundary excludes editing, collection and sending.

requests.complete-request.criterion.3.value: Future verification matches the requested items.

requests.complete-request.body.value: Combine your decisions. Contact should only reveal a fictional address; it must not collect data or send messages. This keeps a simple plan from becoming another system. Mentioned tests are future tests: there is no page to click yet. Read the full request before sending and adapt only details you will still be able to verify.

requests.complete-request.prompt.value: Plan a Ponte Musical page for beginners, with a title, guitar/piano/singing services and a Contact button revealing aulas@example.com without collecting data or sending a message. Return only a list-form plan and explain how to test these items once the page exists. Do not edit files or publish.

requests.scope-check.objective.value: Apply the request’s boundary to an AI suggestion.

requests.scope-check.action.value: Choose an answer and read its feedback.

requests.scope-check.expected.value: Choice justified by the situation’s criterion.

requests.scope-check.hint.value: Use the case information without inventing observations.

requests.scope-check.body.value: Simulated case: before planning, the AI suggests adding login and monthly fee collection. The goal is still a presentation page with contact that sends nothing.

requests.scope-check.check.success.value: You resolved the decision before expanding the work.

requests.scope-check.check.retry.value: Compare the suggestion with the original deliverable and boundaries.

requests.scope-check.option.a.value: Omit login and billing; plan only the requested items.

requests.scope-check.feedback.a.value: This keeps the small deliverable and its defined boundaries.

requests.scope-check.option.b.value: Include every feature so the site looks complete.

requests.scope-check.feedback.b.value: More features change the goal and add unchosen prerequisites.

requests.scope-check.feedback.c.value: Publication was not requested and does not resolve the planning decision.

requests.worked-plan.objective.value: Compare a plan against every request criterion.

requests.worked-plan.action.value: Mark what fits, what is missing and what exceeds scope.

requests.worked-plan.expected.value: Comparison separates correct content, omission and scope change.

requests.worked-plan.hint.value: Check every request item, including the future test.

requests.worked-plan.body.value: Simulated plan: 1) title “Ponte Musical — music for beginners”; 2) guitar and piano services; 3) name/email form that sends a message; 4) check title and sending after building. The title fits; singing is missing; form and sending violate the boundary; verification steps need changing. This analysis concerns text, not files supposedly created.

requests.clarification.objective.value: Resolve ambiguity without expanding the project.

requests.clarification.action.value: Answer the question and explain the chosen behavior.

requests.clarification.expected.value: The answer specifies displaying the address without sending.

requests.clarification.hint.value: Choose an action that can be observed later.

requests.clarification.body.value: Simulated AI question: “Should Contact open email or show the address on the page?” Here, answer that it should display the address without sending. A relevant question clarifies behavior or necessary data; it does not automatically indicate failure. If you do not know yet, choose a smaller scope instead of accepting any assumption.

requests.targeted-revision.title.value: Request a revision that preserves what works

requests.targeted-revision.objective.value: Correct specific points without restarting everything.

requests.targeted-revision.action.value: Write a correction and compare the example revised plan.

requests.targeted-revision.expected.value: The correction keeps the title and fixes omission and sending.

requests.targeted-revision.hint.value: Ask for a specific change and another check.

requests.targeted-revision.body.value: You do not need to discard a plan to fix two problems. Name the omission and unwanted behavior; preserve the correct title. Simulated revision: the plan now lists three services and contact revealing the address; future tests count services and check the click. Reread the revision: a clear request can still produce an incomplete response.

requests.targeted-revision.prompt.value: Keep the title. Add singing alongside guitar and piano. Replace the form with contact that only reveals aulas@example.com. Continue planning only and update tests for the three services and this behavior.

requests.send-and-review.title.value: Try the request in your tool

requests.send-and-review.objective.value: Compare a real response without confusing it with the example.

requests.send-and-review.action.value: Send, compare and record one checked criterion.

requests.send-and-review.expected.value: A received plan and comparison, or an explicit obstacle.

requests.send-and-review.hint.value: Do not push the tool to invent missing details.

requests.send-and-review.body.value: In your prepared tool and folder, send your planning request. Answer relevant questions and compare the plan with your criteria. If it deviates, request revision; if it already fits, record that. Its wording need not match the example. Record the real result or obstacle; simulation does not count as external sending.

requests.plan-evidence.objective.value: Distinguish suitable text from implemented behavior.

requests.plan-evidence.body.value: You received a list containing three services and describing a button that reveals the address. No page has been built or opened in this lesson.

requests.plan-evidence.check.success.value: You recognize the plan’s value without assigning it a nonexistent test.

requests.plan-evidence.option.a.value: The button works with mouse and keyboard.

requests.plan-evidence.feedback.a.value: The list describes behavior but does not execute it.

requests.plan-evidence.option.b.value: The plan covers the items; the button still needs implementation and testing.

requests.plan-evidence.feedback.b.value: This matches the available textual evidence.

requests.plan-evidence.option.c.value: The site is already available to every visitor.

requests.plan-evidence.feedback.c.value: No publication or public-access test was shown.

requests.portable-request.title.value: Deliver a request another tool can understand

requests.portable-request.objective.value: Preserve intent and criteria when changing context.

requests.portable-request.action.value: Record the final request and transfer checks.

requests.portable-request.expected.value: A reusable request with criteria and transfer context.

requests.portable-request.hint.value: The method transfers; interface controls are not necessarily identical.

requests.portable-request.body.value: Keep the request, revised plan and criteria list. For another tool, retain this information and check its folder/context; control names may differ. You do not need another account for this exercise: write what you would preserve and what you would need to check. The next lesson develops test and correction records.

verification.summary.value: Observable criteria, failure reports and retesting.

verification.outcome.value: Compare a result and record a correction with evidence.

verification.evidence-types.action.value: Classify the evidence available in the example.

verification.evidence-types.expected.value: The record identifies a text response and a verifiable time error.

verification.evidence-types.hint.value: 16:00 plus 45 minutes does not require trusting the same AI.

verification.evidence-types.body.value: A “done” message is a claim. An opened file displays content. An observed interaction shows behavior in that test. None guarantees all the others. Here we use a fictional text schedule: a workshop starts at 16:00 and lasts 45 minutes. The simulated response ends at 17:45. We can check the arithmetic without building an application.

verification.success-criteria.expected.value: Criteria include the correct result and what must remain unchanged.

verification.success-criteria.hint.value: Avoid vague criteria such as “looks good”.

verification.success-criteria.body.value: Set four schedule criteria: name “Music workshop”, start 16:00, duration 45 minutes and finish 16:45. The name and start must remain unchanged during correction. Short criteria distinguish fixing an error from changing the agreement. On a site, a criterion could be the address appearing on click; in a report, it could be a calculated total.

verification.baseline.title.value: Record the baseline before changing it

verification.baseline.objective.value: Capture the observation and calculate the expectation.

verification.baseline.action.value: Record observed, expected and the basis for the difference.

verification.baseline.expected.value: The record shows observed 17:45, expected 16:45 and the calculation.

verification.baseline.hint.value: Do not claim a program ran: this is a text example.

verification.baseline.body.value: Simulated example before correction: “Music workshop,16:00–17:45,45 minutes.” Compare start and duration:16:00+45 minutes=16:45. Record the received phrase and the arithmetic supporting the expectation. Keeping this reference avoids relying on memory and helps check whether revision fixed the time without changing the name.

verification.diagnosis-check.objective.value: Provide enough information to locate the problem.

verification.diagnosis-check.body.value: The AI needs to correct the fictional schedule’s finish time while preserving everything else. Which report is most useful?

verification.diagnosis-check.check.quest.value: Choose the report that identifies the error and boundary.

verification.diagnosis-check.check.succe.value: You provided information for a bounded change.

verification.diagnosis-check.check.retry.value: Look for observed behavior, expectation and what must stay unchanged.

verification.diagnosis-check.option.a.value: The workshop ends 17:45. Change the start to 17:00 and keep 45 minutes so the times match.

verification.diagnosis-check.feedback.a.value: The arithmetic would match, but you would change the start that should be preserved.

verification.diagnosis-check.option.b.value: Keep 16:00–17:45 and change the duration to 105 minutes; the arithmetic then works without changing the interval.

verification.diagnosis-check.feedback.b.value: This changes the agreed duration to accommodate the error instead of correcting the finish.

verification.diagnosis-check.option.c.value: “The workshop starts 16:00 and lasts 45 minutes, but the text ends 17:45. Correct it to 16:45 and preserve name/start.”

verification.diagnosis-check.feedback.c.value: The report provides actual, expected, reason and boundary.

verification.reproduction.title.value: Describe how you found the difference

verification.reproduction.action.value: Write three steps to repeat the check.

verification.reproduction.expected.value: Steps connect input data to the observed difference.

verification.reproduction.hint.value: Include the version or passage you actually compared.

verification.reproduction.body.value: Reproduction does not promise an AI will always answer identically. For text, record the request, data and problematic phrase. For a page, record file/address and click sequence. Here the sequence is reading start/duration, calculating finish and comparing it with the phrase. Another person can follow these steps without guessing your reasoning.

verification.repair-request.objective.value: Ask for change while preserving valid criteria.

verification.repair-request.action.value: Write the correction and read the simulated revised response.

verification.repair-request.expected.value: The request specifies the right time and preserves the rest.

verification.repair-request.hint.value: Avoid adding new features during a small repair.

verification.repair-request.body.value: Use your recorded reference to request a precise change. Simulated revised response: “Music workshop,16:00–16:45,45 minutes.” The correction looks right but still needs comparison. The same method applies to an unresponsive button or a report duplicating rows: specify the difference, boundary and test to repeat.

verification.repair-request.prompt.value: Correct only the Music workshop finish time: start 16:00 and duration 45 minutes require finish 16:45. Preserve the name, start and duration. Show the revised phrase and the calculation used.

verification.retest.title.value: Repeat the failed test and preserved criteria

verification.retest.objective.value: Check the correction and its effects on the rest.

verification.retest.action.value: Record each criterion’s result after revision.

verification.retest.expected.value: All criteria have a checked or pending result.

verification.retest.hint.value: Retesting the error and checking preserved behavior complement each other.

verification.retest.criterion.1.value: The revised finish matches the calculation.

verification.retest.criterion.2.value: Name, start and duration were preserved.

verification.retest.criterion.3.value: Pending results were not marked as observed.

verification.retest.body.value: Compare the new simulated phrase with all four criteria: finish 16:45, start 16:00, duration 45 minutes and unchanged name. Merely repeating “is it fixed?” provides little evidence. Recalculate and read. In real practice, use the response or artifact you received; do not mark success if the new version is unavailable.

verification.real-small-change.objective.value: Apply the cycle to a real text change.

verification.real-small-change.action.value: Make the small change and record before/after.

verification.real-small-change.expected.value: The record distinguishes error correction from a requested change.

verification.real-small-change.hint.value: If you cannot run it, complete only simulated analysis and say so.

verification.real-small-change.body.value: In your tool, request and check the same fictional schedule. If an error occurs, use the correction cycle. If it is correct, make a deliberate change: duration becomes 30 minutes, so finish should be 16:30. Label this a new request, not an earlier failure. Compare time and name afterward. Record what actually happened.

verification.verification-limit.title.value: Keep the conclusion within the test

verification.verification-limit.objectiv.value: Report the result and its limits precisely.

verification.verification-limit.body.value: The AI responded “all tests passed”, but you only compared the schedule phrase and its calculation.

verification.verification-limit.check.su.value: Your conclusion is useful because it also states the test’s scope.

verification.verification-limit.check.re.value: Describe observed evidence and what remains outside it.

verification.verification-limit.option.a.value: The checked phrase and calculation are correct; I observed no program tests or publication.

verification.verification-limit.feedback.value: The record limits its conclusion to what was actually checked.

verification.verification-limit.option.b.value: Every app generated by this AI is validated.

verification.verification-limit.feedback.value: A text check does not demonstrate other programs or situations.

verification.verification-limit.option.c.value: No comparison is valid without code access.

verification.verification-limit.feedback.value: You can check text and arithmetic without code; that evidence is useful within its scope.

verification.verification-record.title.value: Take a test record into your next route

verification.verification-record.objecti.value: Organize input, criterion, result and next step.

verification.verification-record.action.value: Complete the record and choose site, app or automation.

verification.verification-record.expecte.value: The record has evidence and a next step for the chosen route.

verification.verification-record.hint.value: A declared obstacle is more useful than invented execution.

verification.verification-record.criteri.value: Remaining work and next route are indicated.

verification.verification-record.body.value: Deliver a short record: input used, criterion, observation, requested adjustment when applicable, retest result and remaining work. In the next routes, use this format with a page, app or CSV. Choose the route matching your goal; automation does not require completing site lessons first. This record supports comparison; it is not automatic certification.

site-build.summary.value: Turn a request into a local page with content and contact behavior you can verify.

site-build.outcome.value: A ponte-site folder with index.html open in a browser and a record of the first tests.

site-build.page-contract.title.value: What this page needs to do

site-build.page-contract.objective.value: Define the content and single interaction of this first page.

site-build.page-contract.action.value: Identify the three services and the only action a visitor will be able to perform in this version.

site-build.page-contract.expected.value: You distinguish showing an address from sending a message or registering someone.

site-build.page-contract.hint.value: The name index.html identifies the initial page; you do not need to memorize code to start.

site-build.page-contract.criterion.2.value: Defines contact as showing the address without sending.

site-build.page-contract.body.value: We will create Ponte Musical, a fictional school for beginners. The page will have a title, guitar, piano and singing offerings, plus a Contact button that reveals aulas@example.com. A static site delivers files to the browser; this exercise fits in one index.html. There will be no form, sending, login or data server. The example and expected results are original Ganesha material; they do not represent a demonstrated execution.

site-build.project-folder.objective.value: Select an exclusive folder before allowing changes.

site-build.project-folder.action.value: Create ponte-site, select it in your chosen tool and record the folder name shown.

site-build.project-folder.expected.value: The tool points to the folder intended only for this page.

site-build.project-folder.hint.value: If the tool shows another folder, adjust the context before requesting file creation.

site-build.project-folder.criterion.2.value: Files from other activities remain outside the scope.

site-build.project-folder.body.value: In Finder or File Explorer, create ponte-site inside your practice folder and select it in your chosen tool. Check its name before requesting changes. If it contains files from another activity, use a new folder. This separation lets you recognize the delivery files and keep changes in the correct project. You do not need to open a terminal for this single-file site.

site-build.project-folder.tool.claude.value: In Claude Desktop, open Code, choose Local and select ponte-site as the working folder. Check the path before requesting changes.

site-build.project-folder.tool.codex.value: In Codex Desktop, open ponte-site as the folder/project and check this context before sending the request.

site-build.plan-page.objective.value: Compare the plan with requested elements and boundaries.

site-build.plan-page.action.value: Send the planning request and note one accepted item and any necessary adjustment to the plan.

site-build.plan-page.expected.value: A plan contains the requested elements and includes no data collection.

site-build.plan-page.hint.value: If the plan already meets the criteria, say so; do not invent a problem to correct.

site-build.plan-page.criterion.1.value: The plan lists all three services and contact.

site-build.plan-page.criterion.2.value: Creation waits for the plan review.

site-build.plan-page.body.value: Send the request below and read the plan before creation. Look for all three services, the contact interaction and the single-file boundary. If the response asks relevant questions, use fictional information. If it suggests registration or sending, ask to remove those features. Your review should connect each proposed element to the intended result without needing to evaluate code.

site-build.plan-page.prompt.value: Plan a Ponte Musical page for beginners in one self-contained index.html: title, guitar, piano and singing, with one clear sentence per service. A Contact button must reveal aulas@example.com, initially hidden, without sending anything. No external libraries, forms, login or collection. Plan for keyboard use and narrow screens. List files and tests. Do not edit or publish yet.

site-build.plan-page.tool.claude.value: Select Plan to request planning without file edits; after reviewing, allow implementation when you are ready.

site-build.plan-page.tool.codex.value: Explicitly ask for planning without editing. Review the response before requesting implementation.

site-build.scope-check.objective.value: Recognize a plan revision that preserves scope.

site-build.scope-check.action.value: Choose the revision that preserves the agreed result and explains the contact boundary.

site-build.scope-check.expected.value: Your choice preserves the services and respects the intended contact action.

site-build.scope-check.hint.value: Compare the visitor action with the agreement at the start of the lesson.

site-build.scope-check.criterion.1.value: Distinguishes showing contact details from collecting data.

site-build.scope-check.body.value: Simulated scenario: the AI proposes three service cards, but replaces the button with a form asking for a name and phone number. You want to preserve the purpose of this first page. Consider what actually needs changing before creating files, without adding a new registration project.

site-build.scope-check.check.question.value: Which response preserves the scope of Ponte Musical?

site-build.scope-check.check.success.value: The plan can now guide creation without introducing registration.

site-build.scope-check.check.retry.value: Return to the requested result: three services and an address shown without collection.

site-build.scope-check.option.a.value: Keep the services and replace the form with the button revealing aulas@example.com without sending.

site-build.scope-check.feedback.a.value: This preserves the three services and corrects the action that exceeded the request.

site-build.scope-check.option.b.value: Keep the form and ask only for a phone number to simplify it.

site-build.scope-check.feedback.b.value: Even with one field, the form still collects information that was not requested.

site-build.scope-check.option.c.value: Remove singing to make space for the form.

site-build.scope-check.feedback.c.value: This removes a required service and keeps the unrequested feature.

site-build.create-html.objective.value: Turn the reviewed plan into an identifiable local file.

site-build.create-html.action.value: Request implementation of the approved plan and record the file the tool reports creating.

site-build.create-html.expected.value: The folder contains a complete index.html without requiring library installation.

site-build.create-html.hint.value: If code appears only in the conversation, ask it to save index.html in the selected folder.

site-build.create-html.criterion.1.value: The result is an index.html file in the correct folder.

site-build.create-html.criterion.2.value: The reviewed plan remains the scope.

site-build.create-html.body.value: After reviewing the plan, request creation. Read the permissions shown by the tool and allow the necessary changes in the exercise folder. The AI may write code and report completion; that does not yet prove the page works. Ask for the name of the changed file and simple opening instructions, preserving the plan boundaries.

site-build.create-html.prompt.value: Implement the revised plan in ponte-site/index.html. Since ponte-site is already the selected folder, save index.html directly there without nesting another ponte-site inside. Include styling and interaction in the file. Preserve all three services and contact without sending. Use a native button with visible focus. Tell me which files changed and how to open the page. Do not publish.

site-build.open-local-page.title.value: Open the file in a browser

site-build.open-local-page.objective.value: Distinguish the rendered page from its file and publication.

site-build.open-local-page.action.value: Open index.html in a browser and record the visible title or the message preventing it from opening.

site-build.open-local-page.expected.value: You see the rendered page and recognize the local file you opened.

site-build.open-local-page.hint.value: Ask the AI for the exact file path if more than one folder has a similar name.

site-build.open-local-page.criterion.1.value: The page was observed in the browser or the obstacle was recorded.

site-build.open-local-page.criterion.2.value: Does not confuse a local file with a public URL.

site-build.open-local-page.body.value: Open ponte-site in your file manager and locate index.html. Use Open with and choose your browser; the address may start with file:. This is the local copy, not a publication yet. If code appears as text, check that you opened it in the browser and that the name did not end in .txt. If the file is empty, return to the tool and request the complete content.

site-build.verify-content.objective.value: Check correspondence between requested and visible content.

site-build.verify-content.action.value: Record the title and three visible services; request a specific correction if any content differs.

site-build.verify-content.expected.value: The observed content matches the requested title, services and boundaries.

site-build.verify-content.hint.value: Example correction: include singing without removing guitar or piano or changing contact.

site-build.verify-content.criterion.1.value: The title and all three services are present.

site-build.verify-content.criterion.2.value: No registration, sending or invented commercial offer was added.

site-build.verify-content.body.value: Compare the open page with the request, not only the AI response. The title must be Ponte Musical, and each service must appear with a sentence beginners can understand. Do not accept missing services or invented promises about prices and outcomes. This check examines content; appearance and accessibility will have their own tests in the next lesson.

site-build.first-contact-test.objective.value: Observe and repeat the page’s main action.

site-build.first-contact-test.action.value: Reload, click Contact and record the actual result, repeating the test after any correction.

site-build.first-contact-test.expected.value: The click reveals the address on the page without sending a message.

site-build.first-contact-test.hint.value: If you did not perform the test, mark it as not performed; an AI response cannot replace it.

site-build.first-contact-test.criterion..value: Compares before and after the click.
Repeats the same sequence after a correction.

site-build.first-contact-test.body.value: Reload the page to start from a known state. Before clicking, the address should be hidden. Click Contact: aulas@example.com should appear without opening a sending action or navigating to another service. Record what happened. If it fails, tell the AI the sequence and expected result, request a limited correction and repeat on the latest saved file.

site-build.first-contact-test.prompt.value: Check index.html: after reloading, the address must be hidden; clicking Contact must show aulas@example.com on the page without sending. I will provide what I observed and whether it failed. If it differs, correct only what is necessary, preserve the three services and explain how to repeat this test.

site-build.evidence-check.objective.value: Limit conclusions to evidence actually available.

site-build.evidence-check.action.value: Choose the conclusion matching the available evidence in this scenario where the file remains unopened.

site-build.evidence-check.expected.value: You limit your conclusion to actual observation without assuming that it works.

site-build.evidence-check.hint.value: Having a file lets you try opening it; it does not reveal the result of a click.

site-build.evidence-check.criterion.1.value: Does not turn an AI message into a behavior test.

site-build.evidence-check.body.value: Simulated scenario: the tool says it created index.html and the button is ready. You located the file but have not yet managed to open it in a browser. Consider file existence, button action and access by other people separately. Each claim requires a different observation.

site-build.evidence-check.check.success.value: Your record distinguishes file creation from verified behavior.

site-build.evidence-check.check.retry.value: Ask what action you actually observed, without substituting the AI message.

site-build.evidence-check.option.a.value: Contact works because the tool confirmed it.

site-build.evidence-check.feedback.a.value: The tool’s confirmation does not show behavior in the browser.

site-build.evidence-check.option.b.value: The page is public because index.html exists.

site-build.evidence-check.feedback.b.value: A local file is not a publication visitors can access.

site-build.evidence-check.option.c.value: The file exists; opening and clicking still need testing.

site-build.evidence-check.feedback.c.value: This records the observation and preserves the checks still needed.

site-build.local-handoff.title.value: Keep the local version and its pending checks

site-build.local-handoff.objective.value: Preserve a local version with identified tests and pending checks.

site-build.local-handoff.action.value: Prepare a short record of the local version and state exactly which test needs to be resumed.

site-build.local-handoff.expected.value: The folder and record let you continue without confusing a pending check with a pass.

site-build.local-handoff.hint.value: Include the real path and your observations; do not copy simulated results as your own.

site-build.local-handoff.criterion.1.value: Keeps an identifiable copy of the folder.

site-build.local-handoff.criterion.2.value: Distinguishes passed, failed and not performed.

site-build.local-handoff.body.value: Keep a copy of the folder before further improvements. Record in plain language the file path, what you checked in the content, the click result and any obstacles. A record such as “click not performed” is valid and guides the next work; it is not a pass. The next lesson checks keyboard use, narrow screens and corrections that preserve existing behavior.

site-quality.summary.value: Test content, contact, keyboard and narrow screens; correct and repeat against clear criteria.

site-quality.outcome.value: A local page with documented essential test results and verified corrections.

site-quality.quality-criteria.objective.value: Define distinct tests for an initial page review.

site-quality.quality-criteria.action.value: Prepare four record rows: content, clicking, keyboard and narrow screen, initially without assigning results.

site-quality.quality-criteria.expected.value: You have distinct criteria and do not declare a pass before performing each test.

site-quality.quality-criteria.hint.value: Use passed, failed or not performed; a pending check does not need a fictional failure.

site-quality.quality-criteria.criterion..value: All four aspects have space for observations.
Recognizes the limits of this initial review.

site-quality.quality-criteria.body.value: A beautiful page can hide a broken button or text that cannot be read in a narrow window. We will check four aspects: content, clicking, keyboard and width adaptation. These original Ganesha exercises are an initial review, not a complete accessibility certification. Each test has an action and an expected result, recorded by the learner.

site-quality.read-as-visitor.objective.value: Find comprehension problems in the locally rendered text.

site-quality.read-as-visitor.action.value: Read the entire page and record one clear passage and any passage needing revision.

site-quality.read-as-visitor.expected.value: Content introduces the school and three services without invented information or leftover instructions.

site-quality.read-as-visitor.hint.value: If everything is suitable, justify a concrete example; do not introduce changes just to complete the activity.

site-quality.read-as-visitor.criterion.2.value: Connects each comment to visible text.

site-quality.read-as-visitor.body.value: Open the local version and read from the beginning through contact, as someone unfamiliar with the fictional school. Check the title, guitar, piano and singing; each description should help a beginner understand the offering without the AI conversation. Look for forgotten sample text, unsupported promises or internal instructions appearing on the page. Note the passage, not just “bad text.”

site-quality.contact-behavior.objective.value: Verify contact across repeated clicks and reloads.

site-quality.contact-behavior.action.value: Perform the click and reload sequence, recording the address and any unexpected page change.

site-quality.contact-behavior.expected.value: Contact reveals the address once without sending and works again after reloading.

site-quality.contact-behavior.hint.value: Compare the open copy with the changed file; an old tab may show another version.

site-quality.contact-behavior.criterion..value: The click neither sends data nor duplicates the address.
The sequence was repeated after reloading.

site-quality.contact-behavior.body.value: Reload and observe the initial state: aulas@example.com should not appear yet. Click Contact and check the revealed address. Click again to check for repeated copies or unexpected navigation. Reload and repeat the first click. This sequence checks the agreed result in common situations; it does not require sending messages, because sending is outside the project.

site-quality.behavior-check.objective.value: Choose evidence demonstrating a visitor action.

site-quality.behavior-check.action.value: Choose the test that provides evidence about the main action beyond the appearance of the button.

site-quality.behavior-check.expected.value: You choose an observed interaction with a result comparable to the request.

site-quality.behavior-check.hint.value: A screenshot from before the click only shows the state before the click.

site-quality.behavior-check.criterion.1.value: Connects a user action to its visible result.

site-quality.behavior-check.body.value: Simulated scenario: the Contact button looks good, the AI wrote “ready,” and you have a screenshot of the initial page. You still need to decide what observation evaluates the promised action. Think about what changes after a visitor acts and how to compare that change with the request.

site-quality.behavior-check.check.questi.value: Which check evaluates whether Contact fulfills its function?

site-quality.behavior-check.check.succes.value: The check provides evidence of the result beyond the button’s presence.

site-quality.behavior-check.check.retry.value: Look for the option combining a visitor action and an observed result.

site-quality.behavior-check.option.a.value: Check that the button color matches the title.

site-quality.behavior-check.feedback.a.value: This checks appearance but does not show whether the address appears.

site-quality.behavior-check.option.b.value: Click and observe whether aulas@example.com appears on the page without sending.

site-quality.behavior-check.feedback.b.value: This action allows comparison of actual behavior with the agreed result.

site-quality.behavior-check.option.c.value: Ask the AI to repeat that the button is ready.

site-quality.behavior-check.feedback.c.value: Another assertion is still not an observation of behavior.

site-quality.keyboard-path.objective.value: Verify keyboard focus and activation of contact.

site-quality.keyboard-path.action.value: Reach Contact with Tab and test Enter and Space, noting visible focus and each activation result.

site-quality.keyboard-path.expected.value: The button can be located and activated by keyboard with a result equivalent to clicking.

site-quality.keyboard-path.hint.value: Focus is the element that receives the next key; if you cannot see it, record that difficulty.

site-quality.keyboard-path.criterion.2.value: Enter and Space reveal the address.

site-quality.keyboard-path.criterion.3.value: No mouse is required to activate the button.

site-quality.keyboard-path.body.value: Reload, click an empty area of the page and put the mouse aside. Press Tab until Contact: an outline or another highlight should show focus. Press Enter and check the address. Reload and repeat using Space when the button has focus. If the button cannot receive focus or activate, request a correction preserving its behavior and label.

site-quality.narrow-layout.objective.value: Evaluate readability and interaction at the tested width.

site-quality.narrow-layout.action.value: Test the page in a narrow window and record clipping, overlap or difficulty accessing contact.

site-quality.narrow-layout.expected.value: Content and button remain readable and usable at the width actually tested.

site-quality.narrow-layout.hint.value: Send the AI a screenshot of the problematic area when possible; add what should appear there.

site-quality.narrow-layout.criterion.2.value: Contact works in the narrow window.

site-quality.narrow-layout.criterion.3.value: The record identifies the tested condition.

site-quality.narrow-layout.body.value: Drag the window edge to make it narrow, roughly a phone’s width. Read the three services and reach Contact. Text should not be cut off, cards should not overlap and the interaction should remain usable. Note the approximate width if known, or describe the window. This window test is an initial check; it does not mean all devices were tested.

site-quality.targeted-repair.objective.value: Request a specific change with boundaries and a repeat test.

site-quality.targeted-repair.action.value: Send a correction based on your observation or a review of results if you found no failures.

site-quality.targeted-repair.expected.value: The request states the condition, expected behavior and what must be preserved.

site-quality.targeted-repair.hint.value: Replace vague judgments such as “improve everything” with a localized problem and a way to check its solution.

site-quality.targeted-repair.criterion.1.value: Uses a real observation or states that no failure was found.

site-quality.targeted-repair.body.value: Choose an actual difference you found and describe how to reproduce it. Original simulated example: in a narrow window, the button sits outside the visible area; the expectation is to reach it without losing services. Do not record this example as your experience. If there is no failure, ask the AI only to review your four results and identify pending tests without unnecessarily editing files.

site-quality.targeted-repair.prompt.value: I will provide my content, click, keyboard and narrow-screen test record for Ponte Musical. For each observed failure, explain the likely cause and make the smallest necessary correction in index.html. Preserve title, guitar/piano/singing and contact that only reveals aulas@example.com. Explain how to repeat the test. If no failure is recorded, only identify pending checks and do not edit on your own initiative.

site-quality.regression-pass.title.value: Retest the change and existing behavior

site-quality.regression-pass.objective.value: Confirm a correction without losing requirements already met.

site-quality.regression-pass.action.value: Repeat the relevant sequence and update each record row with the result you actually observed.

site-quality.regression-pass.expected.value: You know whether the correction solved the problem and preserved the other tested functions.

site-quality.regression-pass.hint.value: If a new failure appears, describe it using the same criteria; do not erase the earlier problem’s history.

site-quality.regression-pass.criterion.1.value: The corrected failure was retested when applicable.

site-quality.regression-pass.criterion.2.value: All four aspects have an explicit result or pending status.

site-quality.regression-pass.body.value: Save or wait for the tool to save the new version and reload the correct copy. First repeat the test that prompted the correction. Then check content, clicking, keyboard and narrow windows: a layout change can affect more than one aspect. If there were no changes, complete only pending checks and record the review. “Fixed” does not end the test on its own.

site-quality.regression-check.objective.value: Identify a regression and guide its correction.

site-quality.regression-check.action.value: Choose the response considering both the resolved defect and the loss introduced by the same change.

site-quality.regression-check.expected.value: You identify that an isolated improvement does not approve a version with a missing requirement.

site-quality.regression-check.hint.value: Compare the new page with all requirements that should remain, not only the latest request.

site-quality.regression-check.criterion..value: Recognizes the need to retest preserved functions and content.

site-quality.regression-check.body.value: Simulated scenario: a change made Contact reachable in the narrow window, but the singing section disappeared. The goal was to fix the layout while preserving all three services. You need to decide whether the new version meets the full criteria and what information should guide the next change.

site-quality.regression-check.check.ques.value: What should happen before considering the version ready?

site-quality.regression-check.check.succ.value: Your review preserves the complete result, not only the latest change.

site-quality.regression-check.check.retr.value: The title, all three services and contact remain part of the agreement.

site-quality.regression-check.option.a.value: Approve it because the button now fits in the window.

site-quality.regression-check.feedback.a.value: The correction solved one issue but removed a required service.

site-quality.regression-check.option.b.value: Remove singing from the criteria to match the page.

site-quality.regression-check.feedback.b.value: This changes the goal to hide a regression instead of correcting the page.

site-quality.regression-check.option.c.value: Ask to restore singing while preserving the width adjustment, then repeat the tests.

site-quality.regression-check.feedback.c.value: This addresses the concrete loss and checks whether both needs are now met.

site-quality.quality-handoff.title.value: Decide whether the page can be published

site-quality.quality-handoff.objective.value: Decide the next step using local results.

site-quality.quality-handoff.action.value: State whether the page is ready for the next step and justify it using your test record.

site-quality.quality-handoff.expected.value: The decision to proceed or correct depends on local evidence and leaves the limits explicit.

site-quality.quality-handoff.hint.value: Example of an honest pending check: keyboard not tested; resume before declaring that criterion passed.

site-quality.quality-handoff.criterion.1.value: Each pass corresponds to an observed test.

site-quality.quality-handoff.criterion.2.value: Failures and unperformed tests remain visible.

site-quality.quality-handoff.body.value: Gather results in a simple record: test, condition, observation and status. A page with blocked contact or missing required content still needs correction. If essential tests passed, keep this folder as the local version you approved. This is neither a complete audit nor publication: the next lesson adds hosting, visitor access and updating.

site-publish.summary.value: Upload a tested version, check access without your session and publish a change in the same project.

site-publish.outcome.value: A URL checked as a visitor or a documented obstacle, with the folder and delivery instructions.

site-publish.local-versus-hosted.objecti.value: Separate hosting from permission for public access.

site-publish.local-versus-hosted.action.value: Identify your tested local version and distinguish hosting files from allowing visitor access.

site-publish.local-versus-hosted.expecte.value: You know publication and public access need their own checks after local testing.

site-publish.local-versus-hosted.hint.value: The administration dashboard URL is not the same evidence as a visitor seeing your page.

site-publish.local-versus-hosted.criteri.value: Distinguishes a local file, hosted URL and public access.
Recognizes that account conditions must be checked.

site-publish.local-versus-hosted.body.value: Opening index.html on your computer shows a local version. Hosting means sending files to a service that provides a URL. Having that URL does not guarantee public access: visibility may require an authorized session. We will use Netlify Drop’s documented procedure without Git or a terminal. This lesson does not claim to publish for you; check pricing, access and permissions in your account.

site-publish.publish-package.objective.value: Prepare a tested package and recognize its version.

site-publish.publish-package.action.value: Prepare ponte-site-publicar with index.html and locally confirm Version A and working contact.

site-publish.publish-package.expected.value: The folder contains the correct page and a visible identifier for the version to upload.

site-publish.publish-package.hint.value: For this self-contained project, index.html is enough; do not add configuration files or credentials.

site-publish.publish-package.criterion.1.value: index.html sits directly in the publication folder.

site-publish.publish-package.criterion.2.value: Version A and contact were observed in the prepared copy.

site-publish.publish-package.body.value: Keep the approved version and make a copy called ponte-site-publicar. Place index.html directly inside the uploaded folder, not inside another nested folder. Ask the AI to add “Version A” in the footer without changing functions. Open this copy and repeat content and contact checks. Upload only page files; leave personal records and files from other activities outside the package. Select ponte-site-publicar as the tool context before editing the copy; preserve the original ponte-site.

site-publish.publish-package.prompt.value: With ponte-site-publicar selected as the project folder, edit index.html directly inside it; do not create another nested folder. Add Version A in the footer. Preserve Ponte Musical, all three services and contact revealing aulas@example.com without sending. Do not publish. Confirm the edited path so I can test this copy locally.

site-publish.hosting-account.title.value: Check the destination account and team

site-publish.hosting-account.objective.value: Identify destination, account conditions and possible blocks.

site-publish.hosting-account.action.value: Confirm the destination account and team or record the condition preventing you from continuing with hosting.

site-publish.hosting-account.expected.value: You identify where the site will be managed and the access conditions encountered.

site-publish.hosting-account.hint.value: Do not include passwords or access keys in the lesson record; identify the account/team in a recognizable way.

site-publish.hosting-account.criterion.1.value: The destination was checked before upload.

site-publish.hosting-account.criterion.2.value: An access block is recorded as pending, not completed publication.

site-publish.hosting-account.body.value: Open https://app.netlify.com/login and sign in or create the account you decided to use. Check the conditions and costs shown before accepting a plan. Choose the team where you intend to manage the project; accounts can have different permissions. This exercise does not require buying a plan. If appropriate access is unavailable, keep the local delivery and record the obstacle without claiming publication.

site-publish.package-check.objective.value: Select the folder matching the approved version.

site-publish.package-check.action.value: Choose the package matching the tested version and the scope of this simple static page.

site-publish.package-check.expected.value: You select the necessary files from the correct version, with the initial page at the expected level.

site-publish.package-check.hint.value: The version identifier helps check the destination later, but it cannot correct an accidentally selected folder.

site-publish.package-check.criterion.1.value: Connects the uploaded folder with the tested local version.

site-publish.package-check.body.value: Simulated scenario: you have the general study folder, an old page copy and ponte-site-publicar, where you tested Version A. You are about to use the upload area. The service needs the page you intend to deliver; choosing a larger folder or a different version can change the published result.

site-publish.package-check.check.questio.value: Which folder should be uploaded in this exercise?

site-publish.package-check.check.success.value: The package matches the version you will recognize at the URL.

site-publish.package-check.check.retry.value: Look for the tested folder with the initial page directly inside.

site-publish.package-check.option.a.value: The general study folder, to include every file from other activities.

site-publish.package-check.feedback.a.value: It can include unrelated material and leave index.html inside subfolders.

site-publish.package-check.option.b.value: ponte-site-publicar, with index.html directly inside and Version A tested.

site-publish.package-check.feedback.b.value: This package matches the prepared page and avoids mixing versions or activities.

site-publish.package-check.option.c.value: The old copy, because the service will automatically apply recent local changes.

site-publish.package-check.feedback.c.value: Upload sends selected files; it does not find changes saved in another folder.

site-publish.first-upload.objective.value: Connect upload, observed result and received URL.

site-publish.first-upload.action.value: Upload the prepared folder and record the received URL or the concrete message preventing publication.

site-publish.first-upload.expected.value: You have a project URL or a documented obstacle without presuming public access.

site-publish.first-upload.hint.value: If the page is blank, check the uploaded index.html and open the same copy locally before correcting the package.

site-publish.first-upload.criterion.1.value: The uploaded folder matches the tested version.

site-publish.first-upload.criterion.2.value: The observed upload result was recorded.

site-publish.first-upload.body.value: With the correct session and team, open https://app.netlify.com/drop and drag ponte-site-publicar into the upload area. Wait for the result and copy the project URL ending in netlify.app. If an error appears or it does not finish, record the message and check connection and folder before retrying. Do not use an empty file to disguise missing content; the page must remain Ponte Musical.

site-publish.visitor-permission.objectiv.value: Check production visibility without changing other policies.

site-publish.visitor-permission.action.value: Check production visibility and make only this project public when that is your permitted intention.

site-publish.visitor-permission.expected.value: The configuration matches the intended audience or the access restriction is clearly recorded.

site-publish.visitor-permission.hint.value: Make public requires a successful production deploy; account role and team policy also matter.

site-publish.visitor-permission.criterio.value: The inspected visibility is for the intended production site.
Missing permissions are not confused with a file failure.

site-publish.visitor-permission.body.value: In the project, check whether production is public or private. When you want public access and your role permits it, use Make public; the documentation also lists Project configuration > General > Visitor access > Project visibility. Production and previews can have separate controls. If the button is absent or team policy prevents it, record the block; do not change settings for the entire team to get around this exercise.

site-publish.visitor-test.objective.value: Verify access and behavior without the owner session.

site-publish.visitor-test.action.value: Test the URL without your owner session and record access, version and main interaction results.

site-publish.visitor-test.expected.value: The intended visitor sees the correct version and can use contact, or obstacles are documented.

site-publish.visitor-test.hint.value: A regular tab can keep your session; confirm the test browser is not authenticated as the owner.

site-publish.visitor-test.criterion.1.value: Access was tested without the owner session.

site-publish.visitor-test.criterion.2.value: Content and contact were checked at the URL.

site-publish.visitor-test.criterion.3.value: The record distinguishes denied access from a defective page.

site-publish.visitor-test.body.value: Open the URL in a private window or another browser without the owner’s Netlify session. Check Version A, the title, all three services and Contact; repeat keyboard and narrow-window tests at this URL. If login or denied access appears, return to visibility and permissions. If content is missing, compare with the uploaded folder. Record what this visitor could actually see and use.

site-publish.publish-update.objective.value: Update the same project and verify the production version.

site-publish.publish-update.action.value: Publish Version B in the same project and check the change and preserved functions at the URL.

site-publish.publish-update.expected.value: The same URL shows Version B and keeps the services and contact working.

site-publish.publish-update.hint.value: If the update breaks something, use the saved copy as the recovery base, test it and upload again to the same project.

site-publish.publish-update.criterion.1.value: The change was tested before reaching production.

site-publish.publish-update.criterion.2.value: The URL shows Version B without losing services or contact.

site-publish.publish-update.body.value: Keep a copy of Version A, change only the footer to “Version B” and test locally. In the same Netlify project, upload the updated folder under Production deploys: this upload changes production, not just a preview. Reopen the same URL as a visitor, check Version B and repeat contact. If the old version persists, check folder, project and upload completion before uploading again.

site-publish.publish-update.prompt.value: With ponte-site-publicar selected as the project folder, edit index.html directly inside it; do not create another nested folder. Change only the footer from Version A to Version B. Preserve all services and contact interaction. Do not publish automatically: I will test and upload the folder to the same Netlify project. Report the changed file and any other difference.

site-publish.public-access-check.title.value: Separate upload success from public access

site-publish.public-access-check.objecti.value: Investigate denied access without confusing it with content failure.

site-publish.public-access-check.action.value: Choose the next step based on the observed difference between the owner’s session and the visitor’s.

site-publish.public-access-check.expecte.value: You check visitor access without confusing it with completed upload or authenticated viewing.

site-publish.public-access-check.hint.value: Uploading identical files again does not necessarily change the policy governing who can access them.

site-publish.public-access-check.criteri.value: Identifies visibility and permissions as relevant investigations for denied access.

site-publish.public-access-check.body.value: Simulated scenario: the dashboard says the update finished and you see Version B while signed in. Someone without your session sees an access restriction screen. We do not yet know which setting imposed the restriction. Choose the appropriate next investigation before announcing that the page is available to any visitor.

site-publish.public-access-check.check.q.value: What is the most useful next action?

site-publish.public-access-check.check.s.value: You keep file transfer separate from permission to view the files.

site-publish.public-access-check.check.r.value: The symptom depends on the visitor’s session; start with access configuration.

site-publish.public-access-check.option..value: Check production visibility and permissions, adjust if allowed and retest without the owner session.

site-publish.public-access-check.feedbac.value: This investigates the access difference and requires confirming the outcome as a visitor.

site-publish.public-access-check.option..value: Announce public access because the dashboard says the upload finished.

site-publish.public-access-check.feedbac.value: Upload completion does not show that an unauthenticated visitor has access.

site-publish.public-access-check.option..value: Remove singing and upload again to eliminate the login block.

site-publish.public-access-check.feedbac.value: Removing a service does not address access configuration and violates the agreed content.

site-publish.delivery-record.title.value: Deliver version, tests and recovery instructions

site-publish.delivery-record.objective.value: Deliver version and evidence with update and recovery instructions.

site-publish.delivery-record.action.value: Write final instructions and deliver the tested URL or the folder with the publication obstacle recorded.

site-publish.delivery-record.expected.value: The delivery identifies the version, observed evidence and a concrete way to update or recover.

site-publish.delivery-record.hint.value: A link alone does not describe which tests passed; add what you actually observed in this version.

site-publish.delivery-record.criterion.1.value: Delivery matches the version actually observed.

site-publish.delivery-record.criterion.2.value: Includes updating the same project and locating the previous copy.

site-publish.delivery-record.criterion.3.value: Pending tasks are not presented as performed steps.

site-publish.delivery-record.body.value: Prepare a short delivery record: URL, observed version, matching folder and results for access, content and contact. Include how to update the same project and where the previous copy is saved. If blocked, deliver the tested folder and exact message without claiming publication. Whoever continues should distinguish what was performed, failed or remains pending; Ganesha does not verify this automatically.

app-state.summary.value: Make a list respond to actions and reject empty input.

app-state.outcome.value: A local app with working add, complete, reopen and remove actions, plus recorded tests.

app-state.state-model.objective.value: Recognize tasks and completion as state.

app-state.state-model.action.value: Describe the expected state after adding A, adding B and completing only A.

app-state.state-model.expected.value: Two tasks: A completed and B pending; neither task removed.

app-state.state-model.hint.value: Separate a task’s existence from its completion mark.

app-state.state-model.body.value: State is the app’s current information: which tasks exist and which are completed. The screen displays that state. Original simulated example: empty list → add A → A pending → complete A → A completed → remove A → empty list. In this lesson, state lasts only for the session; reloading may erase it. Saving for later is the next improvement.

app-state.request-state.objective.value: Set app boundaries before authorizing creation.

app-state.request-state.action.value: Send the request, review the plan and allow creation only inside tarefas-app.

app-state.request-state.expected.value: A plan and index.html with a labeled field, list and requested actions.

app-state.request-state.hint.value: Do not accept login, a data server or synchronization as prerequisites for this prototype.

app-state.request-state.criterion.2.value: Plan stays within the local scope.

app-state.request-state.body.value: Create tarefas-app inside the practice folder and select it in your tool. In Claude Desktop, use Code and the Local context; in Codex Desktop, confirm the active project/folder. Request a plan first and compare its proposed controls with the request. External practice is self-reported: record the response you received or say you have not run it yet.

app-state.request-state.prompt.value: In tarefas-app, plan and then create a self-contained index.html without external libraries. Include a labeled input, Add button, list, complete/undo completion and remove per task. Use unique identifiers, display text as text and reject empty/whitespace input with a clear message without clearing the list. Start in memory only, without login, networking or persistence. Use keyboard-operable controls. Explain changed files and how to test each action. Wait for my plan review before editing.

app-state.request-state.tool.claude.value: In Claude Desktop, open Code and choose Local and tarefas-app; to begin with planning only, choose Plan before sending. Review the plan before allowing edits.

app-state.request-state.tool.codex.value: In Codex Desktop, choose Codex and confirm tarefas-app as the active folder/project. Explicitly request plan review before editing; do not assume Claude’s controls.

app-state.serve-local.objective.value: Open the app over HTTP and stop its server.

app-state.serve-local.action.value: Confirm the folder and Python 3, start the server and record the address and observed page.

app-state.serve-local.expected.value: The browser opens the app over HTTP and you know how to stop the server.

app-state.serve-local.hint.value: Ctrl+C in the server terminal stops it. Port busy: request another port and record the new address.

app-state.serve-local.criterion.3.value: Prerequisite or error recorded without claiming an unperformed run.

app-state.serve-local.body.value: A local server delivers files to the browser while it is running. A terminal is the command area; ask the tool to run inside tarefas-app and show its output. If Python 3 is available, use the command below; on Windows replace python3 with py -3. Open http://localhost:8000. If Python is missing, request an available HTTP preview or specific instructions before installing.

app-state.serve-local.prompt.value: Check whether Python 3 is available and confirm that the working folder is tarefas-app. If available, start the local server for this folder, give the exact URL and explain how to stop it. Otherwise explain an HTTP alternative compatible with my system before any installation. Do not publish online.

app-state.check-empty.objective.value: Validate input without destroying valid tasks.

app-state.check-empty.action.value: Choose the behavior that respects the input and preserves existing work.

app-state.check-empty.expected.value: A rule that distinguishes invalid input from an empty list.

app-state.check-empty.hint.value: Think about what the person can correct and what should remain intact.

app-state.check-empty.body.value: Original simulated scenario: two valid tasks are already visible. A person enters only spaces and presses Add. You need to decide the behavior before implementing it. Consider both the new input and existing data. The response should make the problem understandable without changing valid tasks.

app-state.check-empty.check.success.value: Correct: validation blocks the new input without destroying the list.

app-state.check-empty.check.retry.value: Reconsider the new input and existing tasks separately.

app-state.check-empty.feedback.a.value: That records an entry without content and makes the task hard to identify.

app-state.check-empty.option.b.value: Show guidance and keep both tasks without adding another.

app-state.check-empty.feedback.b.value: This lets the person correct the input and preserves valid data.

app-state.check-empty.option.c.value: Clear the list to start again.

app-state.check-empty.feedback.c.value: Invalid input does not authorize deleting existing tasks.

app-state.add-two.action.value: Add A and B once each and record the count and state after each click.

app-state.add-two.expected.value: One row after A; two after B, both pending.

app-state.add-two.hint.value: If data already exists, use an empty test session or record the initial count.

app-state.add-two.criterion.1.value: Each submission creates exactly one task.

app-state.add-two.body.value: In the open app, add A with one click and then B with one click. Observe the list after each action: first one row, then two. Both should start pending. If one action creates two rows, record the exact gesture and result; a success response in chat does not replace counting the rows.

app-state.toggle-one.title.value: Complete and reopen only one task

app-state.toggle-one.action.value: Complete A, undo its completion and record A and B’s states after both actions.

app-state.toggle-one.expected.value: A switches between completed and pending; B and the count remain unchanged.

app-state.toggle-one.hint.value: Use the control on row A, not a general action for the entire list.

app-state.toggle-one.criterion.1.value: Completion does not remove the task.

app-state.toggle-one.body.value: With A and B visible, complete only A. Its mark should change without removing A or changing B. Undo A’s completion and observe its return to pending. This tests a state transition in both directions. Marking every row or deleting the task does not meet the request.

app-state.remove-target.action.value: Remove B; if it fails, describe the clicked row, request a fix and repeat with two tasks.

app-state.remove-target.expected.value: Only the selected task is removed; the other keeps its state.

app-state.remove-target.hint.value: Ask for the task identifier to be used rather than an incorrect position.

app-state.remove-target.criterion.2.value: Retest includes another task to reveal side effects.

app-state.remove-target.body.value: Remove B and observe A. Only A should remain, with its previous state. Original simulated failure: clicking Remove B deletes A. A useful correction specifies the list order and the row used, while preserving functions that already passed. If your app passes, record the result; do not invent a defect.

app-state.remove-target.prompt.value: In tarefas-app, A and B were in that order. Clicking Remove on B produced [actual result]; I expected only A, with completion unchanged. Fix task targeting, preserve add/complete and explain the change. I will repeat adding A/B, completing A and removing B. If you cannot reproduce it, ask for the missing detail.

app-state.input-keyboard.objective.value: Check empty inputs and keyboard operation.

app-state.input-keyboard.action.value: Test empty input, spaces and keyboard access; record inaccessible controls or unintended changes.

app-state.input-keyboard.expected.value: Empty input is rejected and essential controls work without a mouse.

app-state.input-keyboard.hint.value: Fix one issue at a time and repeat a valid submission after the fix.

app-state.input-keyboard.criterion.1.value: Empty and whitespace input create no task.

app-state.input-keyboard.body.value: With A still in the list, submit an empty field and then three spaces. No row should appear; guidance should be visible and A should stay unchanged. Use Tab to reach the field and buttons. Activate controls with Enter or Space as appropriate for their type and confirm that focus is visible.

app-state.check-regression.objective.value: Recognize side effects of a fix.

app-state.check-regression.action.value: Choose the conclusion supported by both observations rather than the AI’s message.

app-state.check-regression.expected.value: A decision considering both the fixed action and the side effect.

app-state.check-regression.hint.value: Compare every action that the change needed to preserve.

app-state.check-regression.criterion.1.value: Recognizes a regression in required behavior.
