app-state.check-regression.body.value: Original simulated scenario: the AI fixed deletion of the wrong row. Removing B now preserves A, but clicking Complete A deletes A. The AI report says the fix is finished. You need to decide whether the requested set of behaviors still works after the change.

app-state.check-regression.check.questio.value: Does the app now meet the request?

app-state.check-regression.check.success.value: Correct: fixing includes preserving and retesting required behaviors.

app-state.check-regression.check.retry.value: Consider the effect on Complete as well as Remove.

app-state.check-regression.feedback.a.value: One action passed, but completion still violates the contract.

app-state.check-regression.option.b.value: Yes, because the AI declared completion.

app-state.check-regression.feedback.b.value: That claim does not override observed behavior.

app-state.check-regression.option.c.value: Not yet: record the completion failure and repeat add, complete and remove after fixing it.

app-state.check-regression.feedback.c.value: This addresses the regression and checks related functions.

app-state.state-handoff.action.value: Summarize the tests performed and choose the next improvement: keeping data after reloading.

app-state.state-handoff.expected.value: A file and interaction evidence separated from features not yet built.

app-state.state-handoff.hint.value: A documented failure is more useful than marking everything complete without observing it.

app-state.state-handoff.criterion.2.value: Does not infer persistence from one session.

app-state.state-handoff.body.value: Keep a copy of index.html and a record containing address, actions, expected and observed results. Include add, complete, undo, remove, empty/whitespace and keyboard tests. Mark untested when needed. This lesson delivers session interaction, not persistence, login or synchronization. External results are your reports, not automatic platform verification.

app-storage.summary.value: Add local persistence and test reloads, origins and failures.

app-storage.outcome.value: Tasks and completion restored at the same origin, with visible errors and documented limits.

app-storage.memory-storage.objective.value: Distinguish visible state from persisted data.

app-storage.memory-storage.action.value: Explain the difference between seeing A now and finding A after reloading at the same address.

app-storage.memory-storage.expected.value: Two separate pieces of evidence: current interaction and later recovery.

app-storage.memory-storage.hint.value: Keep the same browser and address so test conditions do not change.

app-storage.memory-storage.body.value: The visible list may exist only in page memory. Persistence means saving data to recover later. localStorage holds text in the browser for an origin: protocol, server name and port. Original simulated example: A appears, the page reloads and A disappears. That does not prove adding failed; it means state recovery has not been demonstrated.

app-storage.request-storage.action.value: Send the request, preserve the earlier copy and check the proposed handling of failures.

app-storage.request-storage.expected.value: The plan covers saving, restoring, validating and reporting failures without deleting existing data.

app-storage.request-storage.hint.value: Do not use clearing all localStorage as a fix for an app error.

app-storage.request-storage.criterion.2.value: Dedicated key and complete state specified.

app-storage.request-storage.body.value: Copy the version that passed the tests. Request saving the complete list, including identifiers and completion, and restoring it when opened. JSON is a text representation of data; the app can use it to store the list. Choose a dedicated key, ganesha.tasks.v1, to avoid mixing other exercises at the same origin. Review the plan before changes.

app-storage.request-storage.prompt.value: In tarefas-app, preserve add/complete/undo/remove and validation. Save tasks and completion as JSON in localStorage under ganesha.tasks.v1; restore on opening. Validate the list, unique ids, nonempty text and boolean completion. If reading or writing fails, show a useful message; do not delete invalid data or claim a failed save succeeded. Keep session tasks visible when possible. Explain the plan, format and reload/error tests before editing.

app-storage.reload-state.objective.value: Demonstrate recovery of text and completion.

app-storage.reload-state.action.value: Compare both reloads: first after completing A, then after removing B.

app-storage.reload-state.expected.value: First A completed and B pending; then only A completed.

app-storage.reload-state.hint.value: If nothing returns, record the address and any error before requesting a fix.

app-storage.reload-state.body.value: Open the HTTP address already recorded. Use two fictional tasks A and B and complete only A. Record the exact state and reload in the same browser. Compare count, text and completion. Then remove B and reload again. A list that returns with every item pending saves only part of the required state.

app-storage.check-origin.action.value: Choose the investigation that separates changed context from actual data loss.

app-storage.check-origin.expected.value: A conclusion limited to the address that was actually checked.

app-storage.check-origin.hint.value: Consider the definition of origin before requesting a reset or rewrite.

app-storage.check-origin.criterion.1.value: Recognizes that the port is part of the origin.

app-storage.check-origin.body.value: Original simulated scenario: you saved A at http://localhost:8000. The next server opened http://localhost:8001 and showed an empty list. You have not returned to the earlier address. Before deciding the data was deleted, assess which conditions changed. The number after the colon is part of the tested address.

app-storage.check-origin.check.question.value: What is the appropriate next step?

app-storage.check-origin.check.success.value: Correct: compare the same origin before diagnosing data loss.

app-storage.check-origin.check.retry.value: Notice the concrete difference between the two addresses.

app-storage.check-origin.option.a.value: Return to the earlier origin and check; the port changed, so storage may be separate.

app-storage.check-origin.feedback.a.value: Correct: there is no evidence yet that data at the earlier origin vanished.

app-storage.check-origin.feedback.b.value: That may destroy data and does not explain the changed port.

app-storage.check-origin.option.c.value: Claim the Add function stopped working.

app-storage.check-origin.feedback.c.value: An empty screen at another origin does not test adding in the earlier session.

app-storage.reopen-limit.title.value: Close and return under the same conditions

app-storage.reopen-limit.objective.value: Reopen the app under the same conditions.

app-storage.reopen-limit.action.value: Close and reopen the tab; compare the task and completion using the recorded URL and browser.

app-storage.reopen-limit.expected.value: The task returns under the same conditions, or the failure is described reproducibly.

app-storage.reopen-limit.hint.value: If there is a connection error, first confirm that the server is still running.

app-storage.reopen-limit.criterion.2.value: Connection failure separated from data failure.

app-storage.reopen-limit.body.value: Record the URL and use a regular, not private, window for this test. Close the app tab, reopen the same URL and check completed A. If the server stopped, restart it in the same folder and port. Local storage can be blocked or cleared; it is not a backup, account or cross-device synchronization. Also record the browser used.

app-storage.invalid-storage.objective.value: Verify handling of invalid stored data.

app-storage.invalid-storage.action.value: Run the test copy, observe the warning and confirm that the main key was unchanged.

app-storage.invalid-storage.expected.value: Visible read error, responsive app and preserved main data.

app-storage.invalid-storage.hint.value: If you cannot arrange the rehearsal, record untested and the limitation.

app-storage.invalid-storage.criterion.1.value: Rehearsal isolated from the main key.

app-storage.invalid-storage.body.value: Do not damage valid data to test. Request a test copy with key ganesha.tasks.test and a mode that reads broken JSON only in that copy. This is an identified artificial rehearsal, not a real incident. On opening, the app should report the problem and provide guidance without silently deleting the problematic content or freezing the entire interface.

app-storage.invalid-storage.prompt.value: Create an isolated test copy of tarefas-app using only ganesha.tasks.test. Add an explicitly labeled rehearsal that supplies invalid JSON to the read routine without touching ganesha.tasks.v1 or clearing other keys. I want to observe a readable warning, usable interface and no silent deletion. Explain how to start and remove the rehearsal; do not include this mode in the final delivery.

app-storage.failed-write.objective.value: Observe a write failure and recovery.

app-storage.failed-write.action.value: Observe a rejected write and a later normal write, noting what survives a reload.

app-storage.failed-write.expected.value: The app distinguishes visible data from saved data and demonstrates recovery after the rehearsal.

app-storage.failed-write.hint.value: Do not describe an injected error as a spontaneous browser failure.

app-storage.failed-write.criterion.1.value: Failure is not announced as success.

app-storage.failed-write.body.value: In the test copy, request an intentionally failed write without changing global browser settings. Add C during this rehearsal and observe the message. If C remains visible only for the session, the app must say it was not saved. Then disable the rehearsal, perform a normal write and reload to distinguish the simulated failure from recovery.

app-storage.failed-write.prompt.value: In the isolated test copy, allow a simulated write failure without changing browser settings. When saving is attempted, show that the change was not persisted and keep the interface usable. Explain how to disable the rehearsal. I will then verify a normal write and reload. Do not change the main key or include the test mode in the final version.

app-storage.repair-persistence.title.value: Fix and repeat the entire sequence

app-storage.repair-persistence.action.value: Apply the needed fix or review the passing solution; repeat the complete data cycle.

app-storage.repair-persistence.expected.value: Adding, completing, removing and validation remain correct, including after a reload.

app-storage.repair-persistence.hint.value: A saving fix must not change the input criteria.

app-storage.repair-persistence.body.value: Original simulated example: text returns after reloading but completion disappears. The correction request must name the missing field and preserve adding and removing. Use a real failure from your test if present; if everything passes, request a review of the mechanism and record results without inventing a defect. Also retest removal and whitespace rejection.

app-storage.repair-persistence.prompt.value: In tarefas-app at the same URL, I observed [actual result] after [steps]. I expected text, ids and completion to survive reloading. Inspect saving and restoring; fix only what is needed without breaking add/remove/validation. Explain which data is written. I will retest two tasks, one completion, reload, removal and another reload. If all criteria already pass, explain the mechanism without unnecessary changes.

app-storage.check-save-claim.action.value: Assess the difference between a visible change and a demonstrably persisted change.

app-storage.check-save-claim.expected.value: A report that does not promise recovery after a failure warning.

app-storage.check-save-claim.hint.value: Do not turn an unperformed test into positive confirmation.

app-storage.check-save-claim.body.value: Original simulated scenario: C appears in the list, but the app displays a saving failure warning. You have not reloaded yet. The activity record must describe this state accurately because someone may rely on it when closing the tab. Choose the statement that matches the available evidence.

app-storage.check-save-claim.check.succe.value: Correct: keep current state distinct from saved data.

app-storage.check-save-claim.check.retry.value: Include the failure warning in your evidence.

app-storage.check-save-claim.option.a.value: C is saved because it appeared on screen.

app-storage.check-save-claim.feedback.a.value: The screen shows session state; the warning contradicts a saving guarantee.

app-storage.check-save-claim.feedback.b.value: This app implements neither accounts nor synchronization.

app-storage.check-save-claim.option.c.value: C is visible in this session, but saving failed; recovery is not yet confirmed.

app-storage.check-save-claim.feedback.c.value: This separates the observation from what still needs checking.

app-storage.storage-handoff.action.value: Write a limitations note and preserve the version that passed normal tests.

app-storage.storage-handoff.expected.value: The note explains data location, limits and results without confusing rehearsals with normal execution.

app-storage.storage-handoff.hint.value: Do not use important data before recovery has been demonstrated.

app-storage.storage-handoff.body.value: Record the browser, complete URL, storage key and reload/error results. Deliver the version without test modes. Explain that changing protocol, server, port or browser can lead to a different data area, and browser clearing can remove data. The next lesson creates an exportable copy for moving and recovering tasks without promising synchronization.

app-delivery.summary.value: Export a copy, validate imports and document use.

app-delivery.outcome.value: An app and instructions delivered with a recoverable data copy and controlled replacement.

app-delivery.files-and-data.title.value: Separate the program from its data copy

app-delivery.files-and-data.objective.value: Distinguish the app file from its data copy.

app-delivery.files-and-data.action.value: Identify the two files needed to deliver the program and a copy of fictional tasks.

app-delivery.files-and-data.expected.value: index.html for the app and tarefas.json for exported data.

app-delivery.files-and-data.hint.value: A copy becomes trustworthy only after inspecting its content and testing recovery.

app-delivery.files-and-data.criterion.2.value: Does not call manual transfer synchronization.

app-delivery.files-and-data.body.value: index.html contains the program; browser-local data is not automatically inside that file. Exporting creates a file containing a copy of the tasks. Importing reads that copy to rebuild state. Original simulated example: export completed A and pending B, open another empty instance and import the copy. This is manual transfer, not synchronization or an account.

app-delivery.request-portable.action.value: Review the contract and request export, preview, cancel and confirm-import controls.

app-delivery.request-portable.expected.value: The plan separates reading, validation, preview, confirmation and saving; errors preserve the list.

app-delivery.request-portable.hint.value: Parsing JSON is insufficient: values such as 42 are valid JSON but do not represent this contract.

app-delivery.request-portable.body.value: Request export and import with a simple contract: version equals 1 and tasks is a list. Each task has a unique text id, nonempty text and done set to true or false. Limit this exercise to 100 tasks, titles up to 120 characters and files up to 1 MB. These limits are prototype design choices. Selecting a file alone never replaces data.

app-delivery.request-portable.prompt.value: Add tarefas.json export and import to the app. Format: version:1, tasks with unique text id, text of 1–120 characters after trimming, boolean done; maximum 100 tasks and 1 MB. Validate everything before changing data. Show preview and Cancel/Confirm. Require exporting the current list and confirming the copy was saved before replacement. Update the list only after successful saving; errors preserve current data. Display text as text. No networking. Explain the plan and tests.

app-delivery.export-inspect.action.value: Export and check both tasks and their states; keep the copy unedited.

app-delivery.export-inspect.expected.value: A readable file with version 1, two tasks and completion matching the screen.

app-delivery.export-inspect.hint.value: true means completed; false means pending. Preserve the fields even when task names differ.

app-delivery.export-inspect.body.value: Prepare completed A and pending B. Use Export, locate tarefas.json in Downloads or the chosen destination and open it as text. Compare count, names and done with the screen. Save an identified copy named antes-de-importar.json outside the published folder. The app can initiate a download, but you need to confirm the file was actually saved.

app-delivery.check-contract.objective.value: Separate parseable JSON from accepted data.

app-delivery.check-contract.action.value: Choose how to handle this file before replacing any current list.

app-delivery.check-contract.expected.value: A decision based on the data contract, not only accepted syntax.

app-delivery.check-contract.hint.value: Quotation marks distinguish text from other values in JSON.

app-delivery.check-contract.criterion.1.value: Validates the done type before importing.

app-delivery.check-contract.body.value: Original simulated scenario: a file contains {"version":1,"tasks":[{"id":"t1","text":"A","done":"false"}]}. The reader can parse its syntax. The importer must still check the meaning and types of the fields required by the contract. Look specifically at how the done value is written rather than treating the file extension as sufficient.

app-delivery.check-contract.check.succes.value: Correct: parseable JSON can still violate the app’s contract.

app-delivery.check-contract.check.retry.value: Compare the required type with the quoted value.

app-delivery.check-contract.feedback.a.value: The extension does not guarantee the required shape or types.

app-delivery.check-contract.option.b.value: Replace the list and decide completion later.

app-delivery.check-contract.feedback.b.value: That changes data before validation and may lose the previous state.

app-delivery.check-contract.option.c.value: Reject with an explanation: done must be boolean, not text; keep the current list.

app-delivery.check-contract.feedback.c.value: The contract requires true/false without quotes and preservation on error.

app-delivery.preview-cancel-import.actio.value: Test Cancel first and then Confirm; record the list before, preview and post-reload result.

app-delivery.preview-cancel-import.expec.value: Cancel preserves A/B; confirming the valid copy leaves only pending C after reload.

app-delivery.preview-cancel-import.hint.value: Import in this contract replaces the list; it does not append records or synchronize versions.

app-delivery.preview-cancel-import.crite.value: Selecting a file does not change the list.

app-delivery.preview-cancel-import.body.value: Create a test copy of the exported file containing only pending task C with its own identifier. Keep A/B in the app. Select the file and observe the one-task preview; click Cancel and confirm A/B remain intact. Then select it again, save the current copy and confirm replacement. Reload and compare the new state.

app-delivery.reject-bad-import.objective.value: Reject invalid input without losing data.

app-delivery.reject-bad-import.action.value: Perform all three invalid imports and compare the list before and after each reload.

app-delivery.reject-bad-import.expected.value: Each file fails understandably and C stays pending without changes.

app-delivery.reject-bad-import.hint.value: If the list changes, stop importing and request a fix before using another copy.

app-delivery.reject-bad-import.criterion.value: Wrong type and duplicate id rejected.

app-delivery.reject-bad-import.body.value: In separate copies, rehearse three defects: remove a closing brace from the JSON; make done text; duplicate the same id in two tasks. Try importing each file while keeping C in the list. All must be rejected with a useful reason before replacing any data. Reload after each attempt to check the saved content too. These test inputs are deliberately created.

app-delivery.restore-backup.title.value: Restore a backup and test a rejected write

app-delivery.restore-backup.objective.value: Demonstrate recovery and preservation on error.

app-delivery.restore-backup.action.value: Demonstrate recovery from the copy and behavior during the isolated write failure.

app-delivery.restore-backup.expected.value: The copy restores correctly; a rejected import preserves previous data.

app-delivery.restore-backup.hint.value: If a copy fails validation, keep it intact and record the error before investigating.

app-delivery.restore-backup.criterion.2.value: Failed writing does not replace the list.

app-delivery.restore-backup.body.value: Save a copy of state C and import antes-de-importar.json through the validated flow. Confirm completed A and pending B after reloading. Update the isolated test copy with the current version that already imports files, keeping ganesha.tasks.test. In that copy, simulate a failure while saving an import: preserve the earlier list and warn that nothing was replaced. Disable the rehearsal and repeat a valid import.

app-delivery.restore-backup.prompt.value: Update only the isolated test copy with the current app version, including export/import. In that copy, use only ganesha.tasks.test; do not read, write or remove ganesha.tasks.v1. Then simulate a write failure when confirming a valid import. Preserve the previous list and data, show an error and do not claim replacement succeeded. Explain how to remove the rehearsal. I will test importing the backup, reloading and comparing tasks and completion.

app-delivery.package-handoff.objective.value: Prepare reproducible instructions and a package.

app-delivery.package-handoff.action.value: Request handoff instructions, follow them from the beginning and record whether you delivered a folder or also a URL.

app-delivery.package-handoff.expected.value: Package and instructions allow opening the app and restoring a fictional data copy.

app-delivery.package-handoff.hint.value: Publishing changes the origin: retest reload and import; local data does not migrate automatically.

app-delivery.package-handoff.criterion.2.value: Personal exports excluded from public files.

app-delivery.package-handoff.criterion.3.value: If published, access and behavior tested at the final URL.

app-delivery.package-handoff.body.value: Create README.md covering folder, prerequisites, local command/address, server stop, use, export/import and tests. Keep exported data separate from public files. Static publishing is optional: check Netlify account/cost conditions, upload the folder containing index.html at https://app.netlify.com/drop and verify visitor access. If choosing public access, check permissions and Make public; a URL alone does not prove access.

app-delivery.package-handoff.prompt.value: Create README.md for the final tarefas-app without test modes. Explain opening the folder, checking Python 3 or an alternative HTTP preview, running the server, opening its URL and stopping it. Describe add/complete/remove, local saving, export, checking the copy, import, cancel and recovery. Include A/B tests, no-account/no-sync limits and known failures. List only required public files; exclude my exports. Do not publish automatically.

app-delivery.check-delivery.objective.value: Choose manual transfer without promising synchronization.

app-delivery.check-delivery.action.value: Decide how to transfer data without promising features the app does not have.

app-delivery.check-delivery.expected.value: A manual transfer plan with validation and preservation of the recipient’s state.

app-delivery.check-delivery.hint.value: Sharing the program and sharing a data copy are different actions.

app-delivery.check-delivery.criterion.2.value: Uses validated import with an earlier copy.

app-delivery.check-delivery.body.value: Original simulated scenario: the published app works on the author’s computer. A colleague opens its URL in another browser and finds an empty list. The author wants her to see a copy of fictional tasks, but the app has no account or data server. Choose a solution consistent with what was built and tested.

app-delivery.check-delivery.check.succes.value: Correct: transfer is explicit, validated and manual.

app-delivery.check-delivery.check.retry.value: Separate access to the app from access to another browser’s data.

app-delivery.check-delivery.option.a.value: Send the exported copy; she saves her current data, validates and confirms the import, knowing it will not synchronize.

app-delivery.check-delivery.feedback.a.value: This uses the implemented flow and makes manual replacement explicit.

app-delivery.check-delivery.option.b.value: Ask her to refresh until the author’s list appears.

app-delivery.check-delivery.feedback.b.value: Refreshing another origin or browser does not create synchronization.

app-delivery.check-delivery.option.c.value: Promise that publishing HTML includes all of the author’s local data.

app-delivery.check-delivery.feedback.c.value: Local storage is not automatically embedded in the HTML file.

app-delivery.maintain-version.title.value: Maintain a version you can recover

app-delivery.maintain-version.objective.value: Preserve versions and repeat tests after changes.

app-delivery.maintain-version.action.value: Write what passed, failed and remains untested; record the version and recovery path.

app-delivery.maintain-version.expected.value: The handoff distinguishes evidenced features, limits, a recoverable copy and future precautions.

app-delivery.maintain-version.hint.value: Changing the data format? Plan compatibility before overwriting the only existing copy.

app-delivery.maintain-version.criterion..value: External evidence identified as the learner’s report.
Earlier version and recoverable copy preserved.

app-delivery.maintain-version.body.value: Deliver index.html, README.md and results; share a data copy only if desired. Before future changes, preserve files and export data. Repeat interaction, reload, cancellation and invalid-import tests after every change. If updating through Netlify, test locally first and upload to the same project under Production deploys: this changes the public version. Check the final URL again.

automation-input.summary.value: Define the input, its rules and the expected result before generating a report.

automation-input.outcome.value: A folder with vendas.csv, test copies and a verifiable data contract.

automation-input.pipeline.action.value: Describe this exercise’s input, transformation and output in three sentences of your own.

automation-input.pipeline.expected.value: A map linking vendas.csv to the count, the sum and report.md.

automation-input.pipeline.hint.value: The output is a file; sending that file to someone would be another action.

automation-input.pipeline.criterion.1.value: Names vendas.csv as input and report.md as output.

automation-input.pipeline.criterion.2.value: Includes counting records and summing amount, without sending anything.

automation-input.pipeline.body.value: Automation is a sequence you can repeat. Here, the input is a table of fictional sales; the transformation counts records and adds their amounts; the output is report.md, a text file. First we will define the data and check the result by hand. No script has run, no schedule exists and no report has been sent.

automation-input.create-csv.objective.value: Create and inspect a literal CSV file.

automation-input.create-csv.action.value: Create vendas.csv in relatorio, open it and compare its three lines with the example.

automation-input.create-csv.expected.value: A file with a header and two records, without an extra .txt extension.

automation-input.create-csv.hint.value: If it appears as vendas.csv.txt, request the correct name and open it again.

automation-input.create-csv.criterion.1.value: The id,item,amount header and two records match the example.

automation-input.create-csv.criterion.2.value: The file is in the selected folder and was opened for inspection.

automation-input.create-csv.body.value: CSV is a table written as text: the first line names the columns and each following line is a record. Create the relatorio folder and select it in Claude Desktop/Code or Codex Desktop. Request a UTF-8 text file named vendas.csv with exactly the data below. Open it in the editor and check it; a creation message is not enough.

automation-input.create-csv.prompt.value:
In relatorio, create only vendas.csv as UTF-8 text with the content below, preserving names and decimal points. Do not generate a report, install anything or schedule a task. Show the file path so I can open it.

id,item,amount
1,Caderno,10.50
2,Curso,20.00

automation-input.data-contract.action.value: Write these rules as a list and connect each rule to a column or the table.

automation-input.data-contract.expected.value: A contract that lets you decide whether input is valid before adding amounts.

automation-input.data-contract.hint.value: A row with amount equal to abc violates the value type even with all three columns.

automation-input.data-contract.criterion.value: Includes unique IDs, required fields and the decimal format.
Includes the complete header, at least one record and the limits of this simple CSV.

automation-input.data-contract.body.value: In this original example, the contract is an agreement about what to accept. id identifies a record and cannot repeat; item is a nonempty name; amount is nonnegative, with a decimal point and at most two decimal places. To use the same dataset in both alternatives, omit commas and quotation marks inside names. Incomplete headers and tables without records must cause an error.

automation-input.decimal-check.action.value: Choose the handling that maintains the table contract and makes the problem visible.

automation-input.decimal-check.expected.value: A decision justified by field format before any output is generated.

automation-input.decimal-check.hint.value: Count the comma-separated fields and compare them with the header.

automation-input.decimal-check.criterion.value: Identifies the structural problem without inventing a value.

automation-input.decimal-check.body.value: Consider this simulated line received from someone else: 1,Caderno,10,50. This exercise’s contract uses commas between fields and a point for decimals. Decide what to do before calculating. The line is an assessment case, not an execution by the tool or a change to your original file.

automation-input.decimal-check.check.que.value: How should you handle the line 1,Caderno,10,50?

automation-input.decimal-check.check.ret.value: Compare the field count with id,item,amount and try again.

automation-input.decimal-check.feedback..value: Ignoring a field changes the value and hides an input problem.

automation-input.decimal-check.option.b.value: Accept 10,50 as if a different separator had been configured.

automation-input.decimal-check.feedback..value: The contract has not changed: commas still separate fields. Silent acceptance would make the reading ambiguous.

automation-input.decimal-check.option.c.value: Reject the line and request correction to 1,Caderno,10.50.

automation-input.decimal-check.feedback..value: This restores three fields and the defined decimal format.

automation-input.reference-total.action.value: Count the data lines, add the hundredths and record the total with two decimal places.

automation-input.reference-total.expecte.value: 2 records, 3050 hundredths and a total of 30.50, calculated before execution.

automation-input.reference-total.hint.value: 1050 + 2000 = 3050; divide by 100 to return to the unit.

automation-input.reference-total.criteri.value: Excludes the header from the count.
Records a total of 30.50 and explains its origin.

automation-input.reference-total.body.value: Now calculate the expected result using the two original records. The header is not a sale. To avoid confusion between commas and points, think in hundredths: 10.50 equals 1050 hundredths and 20.00 equals 2000. This original calculation is the reference you will use later; it does not yet prove that any program read the file.

automation-input.failure-fixtures.object.value: Prepare controlled faults without losing the original.

automation-input.failure-fixtures.action.value: Create the two invalid copies and compare each with vendas.csv, which must remain unchanged.

automation-input.failure-fixtures.expect.value: Two identified error inputs and a preserved valid original.

automation-input.failure-fixtures.hint.value: In the copy without a column, remove the corresponding values too; do not change the original.

automation-input.failure-fixtures.criter.value: The original retains exactly the exercise’s two records.
Each copy has one planned fault and a distinct name.

automation-input.failure-fixtures.body.value: An error test should be controlled and reversible. Preserve vendas.csv and create two copies in the folder: vendas-sem-coluna.csv without the amount column, and vendas-valor-invalido.csv with abc replacing 10.50. Do not run a transformation yet. Open each copy and confirm that only the planned change was made; do not use personal data.

automation-input.failure-fixtures.prompt.value: Preserve vendas.csv. Create vendas-sem-coluna.csv by removing amount from the header and its values from the rows. Create vendas-valor-invalido.csv by changing only 10.50 to abc. Do not execute or generate a report. Show all three files for inspection.

automation-input.review-validation.title.value: Review a plan that hides errors

automation-input.review-validation.objec.value: Reject partial output disguised as success.

automation-input.review-validation.actio.value: Rewrite the error rule to prevent partial totals and preserve the last valid report.

automation-input.review-validation.expec.value: A correction requiring a row diagnosis and no replacement whenever an error occurs.

automation-input.review-validation.hint.value: “Improve validation” is vague; say what must happen to an existing output.

automation-input.review-validation.crite.value: Requires an explained error and preservation of the last valid report.

automation-input.review-validation.body.value: Original simulated example: the AI proposes “if a row is invalid, skip it and save the sum of the rest.” That can produce a seemingly correct report containing only some data. Our agreement is to validate all input before replacing any output. Read the plan as a reviewer and request a specific change without claiming execution occurred.

automation-input.prepare-recovery.action.value: Save vendas-valido.csv and record the copy names and reference result each test must respect.

automation-input.prepare-recovery.expect.value: A checked valid copy and a list of files for testing and restoration.

automation-input.prepare-recovery.hint.value: Invalid copies should fail; they do not need a calculated total.

automation-input.prepare-recovery.criter.value: The valid copy has 2 records and an expected total of 30.50.
Distinguishes valid files from tests that should produce errors.

automation-input.prepare-recovery.body.value: Before execution, you need a way back to correct data. Keep a copy named vendas-valido.csv. Open it and check the same reference result. This copy will let you restore input after the tests. If the original is already correct, record that: you need not invent a failure. Recovering data does not mean changing a rule to accept any value.

automation-input.duplicate-check.action.value: Choose how the process should handle two records using the same id.

automation-input.duplicate-check.expecte.value: A decision that respects unique identity and protects the previous output.

automation-input.duplicate-check.hint.value: The program does not know whether a row was duplicated accidentally or an ID should differ.

automation-input.duplicate-check.criteri.value: Applies unique-ID rules without independently deleting or renaming data.

automation-input.duplicate-check.body.value: In another simulated input, two rows use id equal to 1. The item names and amounts differ, but the contract requires unique identification. You are still evaluating input; no report has been generated. Choose a response that lets someone correct the data without silently changing its meaning.

automation-input.duplicate-check.check.q.value: What should happen with two records using id 1?

automation-input.duplicate-check.check.s.value: You preserved information and made the error correctable.

automation-input.duplicate-check.check.r.value: Consider who can decide the correct identity of each record.

automation-input.duplicate-check.option..value: Report the repeated ID, preserve the valid report and request corrected input.

automation-input.duplicate-check.feedbac.value: This exposes the ambiguity and leaves correction to someone who knows the data.

automation-input.duplicate-check.option..value: Automatically rename the second ID to 2 and continue.

automation-input.duplicate-check.feedbac.value: This may assign the wrong identity without confirmation of the data.

automation-input.duplicate-check.option..value: Discard the second row and sum only the first.

automation-input.duplicate-check.feedbac.value: Silent removal may lose a valid sale and produce an incomplete total.

automation-input.handoff-input.objective.value: Document the input package and its limits.

automation-input.handoff-input.action.value: Deliver the folder and a short record separating checked files, reference results and tests not yet run.

automation-input.handoff-input.expected.value: An input package another person can understand, with clear evidence limits.

automation-input.handoff-input.hint.value: If you worked only in simulation, say so and retain the same criteria.

automation-input.handoff-input.criterion.value: Includes the contract, valid file, test copies and reference result.
Does not claim transformation execution before performing it.

automation-input.handoff-input.body.value: Gather the valid file, error copies and contract. Write that the expected result is 2 records and total 30.50, while invalid copies must produce a diagnosis and preserve valid output. Record which files you actually opened. This completes data preparation; the next lesson runs the transformation without requiring the site or app routes.

automation-report.summary.value: Run, compare, trigger a controlled error and recover without duplicating data.

automation-report.outcome.value: A checked report with evidence of normal execution, repetition, error handling and recovery.

automation-report.execution-paths.title.value: Choose how to run the transformation

automation-report.execution-paths.action.value: Choose Python or HTML and explain where input will be read and output will go.

automation-report.execution-paths.expect.value: A defined execution route with a way to save and compare output.

automation-report.execution-paths.hint.value: You do not need to install Python to use the HTML alternative.

automation-report.execution-paths.criter.value: Distinguishes a file replaced by the script from a browser download.
Keeps the same data contract in both routes.

automation-report.execution-paths.body.value: You can use Python 3 to generate report.md directly in the folder, or a local HTML page to paste CSV, inspect a preview and download the report. The data rules are the same. The script can replace the file after validation; the browser offers a download and does not automatically replace previously downloaded files. Choose a route and identify this distinction.

automation-report.environment.action.value: Request an environment check and record the folder, command and version or obstacle.

automation-report.environment.expected.value: Evidence of available Python, or an explicit HTML choice without claiming Python execution.

automation-report.environment.hint.value: “Command not found” is useful environment information, not a fault in the sum.

automation-report.environment.criterion..value: The folder contains vendas.csv and the test copies.
Records observed check output or states that the check was not run.

automation-report.environment.body.value: A terminal is the area where commands run; your assistant can run them and show output. Open relatorio in Claude Desktop/Code or Codex Desktop and request checks of the folder, files and Python 3. Use `python3 --version`; on Windows use `py -3 --version`. If unavailable, record the obstacle and choose HTML without installing anything automatically.

automation-report.environment.prompt.value: Check the relatorio folder and list vendas.csv and the test copies. Check Python 3 with `python3 --version`, or `py -3 --version` on Windows. Show the output. Do not install or schedule anything. If unavailable, propose the local HTML alternative.

automation-report.build-transform.object.value: Turn rules into an implementable request.

automation-report.build-transform.action.value: Send your route’s request, review the plan and authorize the files after checking the rules.

automation-report.build-transform.expect.value: report.py or report.html created in the folder, with usage instructions and no schedule.

automation-report.build-transform.hint.value: For HTML, explicitly request that no data be sent over the network.

automation-report.build-transform.criter.value: Validates all input before updating output.
Includes error and repetition rules and preserves vendas.csv.

automation-report.build-transform.body.value: Ask for a plan first and read how it validates all input, calculates the total and handles errors. Then authorize creation of your chosen version. For Python, the command takes input and output arguments. For HTML, request a CSV paste area, preview, error message and download. These requests describe work to perform; they are not proof of a finished program.

automation-report.build-transform.prompt.value: In relatorio, plan then create report.py in Python 3 without external packages, taking input/output arguments; without Python, use report.html with CSV pasting, preview and download. CSV: id,item,amount; unique IDs, nonempty item, nonnegative amount with decimal point and at most two decimals; names without commas/quotes. Reject extra/missing fields and empty tables. Validate everything before counting and decimal summation. Preserve input and valid output on error; repetition never accumulates. No network/scheduling. Wait for plan review before editing; explain execution.

automation-report.path-check.action.value: Choose an investigation that compares the command with the file’s actual location and name.

automation-report.path-check.expected.value: A next step that checks context without changing data to hide the error.

automation-report.path-check.hint.value: A correct filename in another folder may still be unavailable to the current command.

automation-report.path-check.criterion.1.value: Investigates folder and path before modifying calculations or data.

automation-report.path-check.body.value: Original simulated example: the command says vendas.csv was not found. You know a copy exists on the computer but have not checked where the command is running. Choose a useful first investigation. This error occurs before reading the records; it does not yet support any conclusion about the addition formula.

automation-report.path-check.check.quest.value: The command cannot find vendas.csv. What should you check first?

automation-report.path-check.check.succe.value: You investigated execution context before changing the transformation.

automation-report.path-check.check.retry.value: Separate finding a file from interpreting its contents.

automation-report.path-check.option.a.value: Replace 10.50 with 0 to simplify the calculation.

automation-report.path-check.feedback.a.value: The program has not read the file yet; changing values cannot fix its path.

automation-report.path-check.option.b.value: Check the current folder, exact filename and path passed to the command.

automation-report.path-check.feedback.b.value: This checks whether the command is looking for the file in the correct place.

automation-report.path-check.option.c.value: Create an empty report and consider the task complete.

automation-report.path-check.feedback.c.value: Empty output does not replace execution with the required input.

automation-report.normal-run.objective.value: Compare actual output with the reference.

automation-report.normal-run.action.value: Run your chosen route, open report.md and compare its count and total with the previous lesson’s reference.

automation-report.normal-run.expected.value: Observed output with 2 records and total 30.50, or a precisely described obstacle.

automation-report.normal-run.hint.value: Also confirm that vendas.csv still contains the three original lines.

automation-report.normal-run.criterion.1.value: Opens output and compares two values rather than relying only on the AI message.

automation-report.normal-run.criterion.2.value: Distinguishes expected results from execution actually observed.

automation-report.normal-run.body.value: For Python, run `python3 report.py vendas.csv report.md` inside relatorio; on Windows use `py -3 report.py vendas.csv report.md`. For HTML, open report.html in the browser, paste the exact data and generate the preview. If opening fails, request an available local preview and record the obstacle. Compare 2 records and 30.50 before saving or downloading, then open the output.

automation-report.repeat-run.action.value: Repeat the transformation and compare its count, total and rows with the first output.

automation-report.repeat-run.expected.value: The same content result without accumulated records or totals.

automation-report.repeat-run.hint.value: A file called report (1).md may be a new download; open it before choosing a version.

automation-report.repeat-run.criterion.1.value: The second run keeps 2 records and total 30.50.

automation-report.repeat-run.criterion.2.value: Identifies the file or preview that was compared.

automation-report.repeat-run.body.value: Run again with the same input. The count must remain 2 and the total 30.50; the report must not gain a second copy of the records. In Python, compare the replaced file. In HTML, compare the preview before downloading: the browser may give a download another name, which does not mean the program updated the previous file.

automation-report.error-run.title.value: Test errors without losing valid output

automation-report.error-run.action.value: Run both invalid inputs and compare the valid output before and after each attempt.

automation-report.error-run.expected.value: Two visible errors without losing the valid report or replacing it with a partial sum.

automation-report.error-run.hint.value: If the program overwrites output on error, record the behavior before requesting a fix.

automation-report.error-run.criterion.1.value: The missing column and abc value produce a diagnosis.

automation-report.error-run.criterion.2.value: The valid Python file or HTML preview remains preserved.

automation-report.error-run.body.value: First use vendas-sem-coluna.csv, then vendas-valor-invalido.csv, preserving vendas.csv. In Python, change only the input argument and keep report.md as output. In HTML, paste one invalid copy at a time. Each attempt must show the problem and keep the last valid result; do not accept a partial sum. In the browser, keep the tab open and do not download a replacement after an error.

automation-report.recover-retest.objecti.value: Test a valid change and return to original data.

automation-report.recover-retest.action.value: Record actual failures or success, test the 31.50 variation and restore the original 30.50 case.

automation-report.recover-retest.expecte.value: Checked recovery and a final report matching the original data.

automation-report.recover-retest.hint.value: Do not invent a failure: the valid variation already lets you observe a changed result.

automation-report.recover-retest.criteri.value: The variation keeps 2 records and changes only the expected total to 31.50.

automation-report.recover-retest.body.value: If a test failed, send the input, steps, result and expected rule; request a narrow correction and repeat normal, repetition and error tests. If all passed, record that. Then create a valid variation replacing 10.50 with 11.50: expect 2 records and 31.50. Finally restore the original input and check 30.50; this tests an update and a return.

automation-report.recover-retest.prompt.value: When running [input and steps], I observed [actual result]; I expected [contract rule]. Fix only the cause, preserve already-passing rules and explain what changed. Then repeat normal, repetition and error tests. Do not declare success without showing the results.

automation-report.download-check.action.value: Choose the action that confirms deliverable content without assuming the browser overwrote a file.

automation-report.download-check.expecte.value: An identified file checked as the version to be delivered.

automation-report.download-check.hint.value: A preview and a previously downloaded file are different objects.

automation-report.download-check.criteri.value: Requires opening the current download and checking its contents.

automation-report.download-check.body.value: Original simulated example: using HTML, you generated a 31.50 preview, but report.md open in the editor still contains 30.50. The page was not authorized to replace files on disk. Choose how to identify the current deliverable. An old file remaining open is not, by itself, evidence of a calculation error.

automation-report.download-check.check.q.value: The HTML preview changed but the old report.md did not. What should you do?

automation-report.download-check.check.s.value: You distinguished the page result from the delivered file.

automation-report.download-check.check.r.value: Consider which file another person will receive and open.

automation-report.download-check.option..value: Declare that the old file was updated automatically.

automation-report.download-check.feedbac.value: A new preview does not by itself modify a file already on disk.

automation-report.download-check.option..value: Manually add both reports to combine the runs.

automation-report.download-check.feedbac.value: That would duplicate data from versions meant to replace one another.

automation-report.download-check.option..value: Download the current version, check its name and contents, and deliberately choose the delivery file.

automation-report.download-check.feedbac.value: You verify the actual artifact without confusing a preview with file replacement.

automation-report.deliver-report.title.value: Deliver a process someone can repeat

automation-report.deliver-report.action.value: Prepare a delivery note with files, command or HTML workflow, reference result and evidence from all four tests.

automation-report.deliver-report.expecte.value: A repeatable package with checked output and explicit limits, ready for a scheduling discussion.

automation-report.deliver-report.hint.value: For HTML, explain where to paste data and how to select the correct download.

automation-report.deliver-report.criteri.value: Instructions let someone repeat the chosen route.
Tests and obstacles are reported without presumed execution.

automation-report.deliver-report.body.value: Gather vendas.csv, your chosen program and report.md. Add opening or execution instructions, the folder used and normal, repetition, error and recovery test results. Explain the limits: fictional data, simple CSV format and no schedule or message sent. If something did not run, record why. A useful delivery lets someone repeat the process and recognize failures.

automation-schedule.summary.value: Plan timing, context and follow-up without confusing configuration with execution.
